To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the best way to present a multiparameter display is in isometric projection; (2) the best way for the viewer to perceive a multiparameter isometric display is to use a logarithmic intensity modulation technique; (3) to obtain a logarithmic intensity modulated display, the matrix CRT must have a high resolution and a high frame rate, and the CRT must be operated with a large spot size.
the best matrix spot intensity modulation technique is a logarithmic modulation of matrix spot intensity in proportion to picture content.

1) the best intensity modulation function is the square root of contents; 2) the best intensity function for isometric displays is contents to the 1/3 power; 3) a 100 spot per line matrix is adequate for most purposes; 4) a 30 Hz frame rate is adequate for most display purposes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of techniques to enhance the visual effectiveness of multiparameter displays.
the visual perception of multiparameter displays and the design of displays that will provide the most useful information to the operator.
the development and evaluation of techniques for the presentation of multiparameter information in pictorial form.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the intensity modulation technique which provides best data picture quality and viewing comfort is a combination of linear and logarithmic spot intensity modulation, with the linear modulation providing the 3-dimensional isometric illusion, and the logarithmic modulation providing the best detail and high light contrast.

intensity modulated multiparameter displays can be made to appear 3-dimensional, and that the intensity modulations should be logarithmic, and not linear, in order to provide good picture quality under high ambient light conditions.
the best results are achieved by using a CRT with 0.5 to 0.7 mm spot size, and by using a logarithmic intensity modulation technique.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
multiparameter displays can be made to appear 3-dimensional, and can also be made to provide improved data picture quality, but at the expense of increased CRT spot size.

the multiparameter display is a viable concept, and that it is possible to obtain acceptable data picture quality and viewing performance with a CRT matrix display, using a 3- to 6-inch diagonal screen.
multiparameter displays can be made to appear quite natural and realistic, and can be made to perform well in the presence of high ambient light levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intensity of a display element should be proportional to the logarithm of the value of the data element.
the intensity of the matrix spot should be proportional to the contents of the display, and that the intensity should be modulated logarithmically.
the intensity of the spots should be modulated in direct proportion to the contents.
